**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fail readiness for observed rate-limit store errors**

When `RATE_LIMIT_FAILURE_MODE=fail_closed` and `SharedRateLimitStore.consume` throws, `consumeRateLimitViaStore` records a `degrade_reason` with `degraded:false` before rethrowing. This check only reacts to `degraded === true`, so `/api/readiness` can continue returning `200 ready` whenever the read projection probe passes, even though rate-limited routes are failing closed with server errors. Treat an observed shared-store error/degrade reason as a failed readiness check.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Respect alias env vars in profile-required checks**

For deployments that use the already-supported aliases, this literal required-key pass fails before the alias-aware validators can satisfy the same dependency: for example `SUPABASE_DB_URL`/`SUPABASE_DATABASE_URL` still pass `validateDatabaseUrl()`, but `thin_v1` and `full_rag` now report `DATABASE_URL:missing_required`; `full_rag` similarly rejects embedding aliases such as `EMBEDDING_API_KEY`/`DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` because `VECTOR_EMBEDDING_API_KEY` is required literally. This regresses supported production env shapes unless the matrix can express alias groups or these keys are removed from the literal required list.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disable provider-dependent RAG routes for thin_v1**

For `thin_v1`, this skips provider credential validation while the profile also forbids those credentials, but I checked `api/_runtime/route-registry.js:199-218` and `/api/rag/search` plus `/api/rag/ask` are still registered unconditionally; those handlers call the embedding path, which returns `RAG_EMBEDDING_KEY_MISSING` when provider keys are absent. A thin deployment can therefore pass preflight/readiness but still expose authenticated RAG endpoints that fail at runtime instead of being disabled or excluded for the profile.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
